title: Drop the cut in writing-down allowances
name: Drop the cut in writing-down allowances
headline: Drop allowances cut. Costs £1.1bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2027 the main writing-down allowance falls from 14% to 12%, while the first-year allowance rises from 40% to 50% from January 2027. Firms deduct less of their plant and machinery each year. Switch this on to drop the change.

baselinePolicy.text: The main rate writing-down allowance is 12% from April 2027 and the first-year allowance 50% from 1 January 2027 (Table 6.1 line 58).

source.quote: This measure reduces the main rate Writing Down Allowance (WDA) for capital allowances from 14% to 12% and increases the first-year allowance (FYA), announced at Autumn Budget 2025, from 40% to 50%.

alreadyIncludes: The main rate writing-down allowance is 12% from April 2027 and the first-year allowance 50% from 1 January 2027 (Table 6.1 line 58).

lines.title: Writing-down Allowances: Reduce the main rate writing-down allowance to 12% from April 2027 and increase the main rate first-year allowance to 50% from 1 January 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
